findings: The controller is prefix-causal, honors pause/cancel and preserves one primary arm under these controlled intents.
Bounded native-curve retiming and a small persistent posture state are executable on the actual Cubism asset.
The neutral and quoted controls remain motionless despite acoustic accents and gesture words.
These checks demonstrate mechanisms, not improved naturalness or semantic generalization.
No word-level emphasis alignment, learned timing model or seamless native-arm handoff has been validated.
limitations: Audio was fully synthesized before offline rendering, so this is not a live latency benchmark.
Authored semantic intents are controlled experimental inputs, not training labels or model predictions.
RMS-onset accents are acoustic proxies, not verified word-level semantic emphasis.
Posture continuation is restricted to small torso/head offsets; native arm handoffs remain unchanged.
No human motion ground truth; movement magnitude and lower jerk alone do not prove naturalness.
latency_scope: Offline local-policy timing only. Rendering ran after releasing TTS/4B workers; no concurrent or first-audio latency claim.
